quotes.text: The thing about a filibuster is — and I say this as someone who has both conducted one and survived one — it is a profoundly humbling experience. You run out of interesting things to say around hour four. After that you're basically just reading a phone book with conviction.
quotes.speaker: Ted Cruz
quotes.context: Panel discussion at the Texas Tribune Festival, Austin, Texas, September 2018
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Cruz famously conducted a 21-hour filibuster in 2013, including reading Green Eggs and Ham, so he has genuine material to draw from here. The giveaway is 'with conviction' as the kicker; his real self-deprecation about that episode tends to be a little more defensive.

quotes.text: Washington runs on acronyms. I have been in this city long enough that I sometimes think in acronyms. My wife has asked me to stop.
quotes.speaker: Chuck Hagel
quotes.context: Keynote remarks at the Atlantic Council Distinguished Leadership Awards, Washington D.C., April 2014
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Hagel, a Defense Secretary who spent decades in government, had a plain-spoken, gently self-deprecating manner in public addresses, and the bureaucratic-jargon observation is entirely consistent with his known speaking style. The giveaway is the wife detail, which is a stock aside he might have avoided in a formal setting.

quotes.text: The disappointment of manhood succeeds to the delusion of youth: let us hope that the heritage of old age is not despair.
quotes.speaker: Benjamin Disraeli
quotes.context: The British Prime Minister and novelist, in a candidly reflective aside on the disappointments of the ages of life (from his fiction, Book VIII, Chapter 4).

quotes.text: Where my reason, imagination or interest were not engaged, I would not or I could not learn.
quotes.speaker: Winston Churchill
quotes.context: From Churchill's own autobiography 'My Early Life: A Roving Commission' (1930), in the chapter recalling his schooldays at Harrow where he was placed in the lowest form.

quotes.text: I am a Ford, not a Lincoln. My addresses will never be as eloquent as Mr. Lincoln's. But I will do my very best to equal his brevity and his plain speaking.
quotes.speaker: Gerald Ford
quotes.context: Self-deprecating remark Ford made on December 6, 1973, immediately after taking the oath of office as the 40th Vice President (following Spiro Agnew's resignation).

quotes.text: I grew up in a small town where the city council meetings were the main civic event of the month. People brought snacks. There were feuds. It was, genuinely, more dramatic than anything I have encountered in the Senate, and I want to be careful about how I say that.
quotes.speaker: Jon Tester
quotes.context: Interview on Montana Public Radio, Great Falls, Montana, August 2018
